title: C3, C4 or CAM?
caption: C3 plants fix CO₂ directly with RuBisCO. C4 and CAM plants first fix CO₂ into a four-carbon acid with PEP carboxylase, which does not bind oxygen, and release it near RuBisCO. C4 separates the steps in space (mesophyll and bundle sheath cells); CAM separates them in time (night and day).
alt: A flow chart: no four-carbon acid means C3; a four-carbon acid with steps in different cells means C4; with steps at different times means CAM.
description: Does the plant first fix CO₂ into a 4-carbon acid? If not, it is C3: RuBisCO fixes CO₂ directly.
If so, are the steps in different cells, mesophyll and bundle sheath? If so, it is C4: separated in space, as in maize.
If not, they are at different times: CAM, as in cacti. Stomata open at night and malate is stored; by day the stomata close and malate releases CO₂.

q1.q: Does the plant first fix CO₂ into a four-carbon acid (with PEP carboxylase)?

c3.outcome: C3: RuBisCO fixes CO₂ directly in the Calvin cycle

q2.q: Are the steps in different cells: mesophyll, then bundle sheath?

c4.outcome: C4: steps separated in space. Maize, sugarcane; good in hot, sunny, dry conditions

cam.outcome: CAM: steps separated in time. Stomata open at night: cacti, pineapples
